title: James son of Zebedee
aliases: who is james son of zebedee
tell me about james son of zebedee
why is james son of zebedee important
summary: Matthew depicts James son of Zebedee at work in a fishing boat with his brother John and their father when Jesus calls them. Luke later names James among the Twelve, and Acts includes him among the disciples gathered in Jerusalem. The cited scenes show his call and place in the group, but do not describe his later ministry.
historical_context: Matthew 4:18–22 places James in a family fishing business with his brother John and their father Zebedee at the time of his call. Luke 6 and Acts 1 then name him among the Twelve and the gathered disciples. These passages establish a brief outline, not a full chronology of his life.
ancient_near_east_context: The call scene mentions a boat, fishing work, and James’s father and brother; those details make clear that following Jesus meant leaving an existing family work setting. The text does not provide enough information to generalize about the economics or customs of all fishing households.
canonical_context: In these references James is identified as Zebedee’s son and as one of the Twelve. The texts give more detail about his call than about his later actions, so accounts of his subsequent ministry should not be inferred from these passages alone.
literary_context: The references move from call to group identity: Matthew 4 shows James and John leaving their boat and father to follow Jesus, Luke 6 names James when Jesus appoints the Twelve, and Acts 1 places him among the disciples after Jesus’ departure. The pattern highlights both the personal cost narrated at the call and James’s later place within a larger group.
covenantal_significance: The cited passages connect James with Jesus’ call and with the Twelve, the group that represents the renewed community gathered around Jesus. They support this role in the Gospel and Acts narratives, but do not describe a distinct teaching or later mission for James in the passages listed here.
canonical_role: James son of Zebedee serves as a canonical person anchor, connecting biographical context, key passages, and related places, events, and themes.

interpretive_notes.note: The apostolic role is about witness and commission, not private spiritual status.
The Gospels and Acts often show both calling and ongoing formation.
